title: Decision output at the padded time bound
statement: Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine, $L$ a language of finite binary words, $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and $a\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input $x$, $M$ halts within $aT(|x|)$ steps, outputs the single bit indicating whether $x\in L$, and uses some finite amount of work space. Then after $(a+1)(T(|x|)+1)$ steps on any input $x$, the last output bit, interpreted as false if the output is empty, equals the indicator of whether $x\in L$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$L$ is a language of finite binary words
replaced:
Let $M$ be a binary machine that decides a language $L$ over the binary alphabet
within time $a \cdot T(n)$ on inputs of length $n$.  Then for every input $x$, after
running $M$ for $(a + 1)(T(|x|) + 1)$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, the
last bit of the output word, defaulting to false, equals the indicator of the
membership of $x$ in $L$.
